article.title: Agenda for a Democratic Congress
article.author: John Peeler
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. When Democratic majorities take office in January (if indeed Trump doesn’t find a way to stop them from claiming the fruits of victory), the country will be prostrate. The damage will take years to repair. But next year’s Democratic Congress must make the case that the Democrats deserve a chance to govern. Investigate, surely, but also legislate. Trump will veto any law they enact. But only by forcefully laying out their policies can they make the case for a Democratic President in 2028. The first priority must be to abolish Immigrations and Customs Enforcement and the dismiss the thousands of hastily recruited and poorly trained agents that have terrorized communities across the country. ICE is broken and must be replaced. At the same time, Democrats need to pass a comprehensive immigration reform based on these principles: We need immigrants; We have a right to control our borders; Immigration should always be legal and should always have a path to citizenship. Related: Will Trump Take Cuba? The Centers for Disease Control must regain its status as the premier public health agency in the country, and must vigorously counter the anti-vaccine hysteria perpetrated by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The Right-Wing hostility toward scientific expertise must be repudiated. Trump has assaulted all aspects of environmental policy. A Democratic Congress must rectify this attack on the environment. From getting back to confronting climate change, to exercising control over environmental pollutants, the list of environmental challenges is daunting. Democracy itself is in urgent need of repair. This will not be easy, for the MAGA storm troopers will continue to question every adverse election result. But we need to get back to a political order where electoral results depend on vote counts, no matter the outcome, and where the claim of fraud when one loses is no longer acceptable. These are just the most prominent and urgent challenges confronting a Democratic Congress. Many other issues will also force themselves on our attention. Among these will be the many hundreds of Executive Orders enacted by Trump. Legislative action can override an executive order. Trump would have to veto each congressional bill that would override one of his executive orders. His many vanity projects (most notably the Ballroom, the Arc de Trump) all irregularly financed, beg to be reined In. Related: Is Republican Solid South Beginning to Crack? Trump’s reign has been equally damaging abroad. The “rules-based international order” lies in tatters as he pursues a backward-looking vision of spheres of influence. Thus we have Venezuela decapitated and its Vice President subject to the whim and will of Marco Rubio, effectively the American Viceroy. Meanwhile, Trump keeps trying to find a way to hand Ukraine to Russia, and to look the other way as China attacks Taiwan. Power rules. But ironically, Trump has dissolved US power in the world. Iran makes the point. Trump and Netanyahu chose to attack Iran, even though it’s outside the US sphere of influence. Netanyahu is quite content to keep fighting, since that helps keep him in power, but Trump wants a way out of an unpopular war, and can’t find it. It is his Tar-Baby. Trump has systematically sucked up to his authoritarian rivals. Xi and Putin, while trashing our traditional allies. The US is increasingly isolated on the world stage, and Trump can no longer threaten his allies. Among the most shockingly self-destructive acts was the demolition of the Agency for International Development (AID). For a few billion dollars a year, we saved lives, and helped people to stay home rather than emigrating. It was soft power at its best, and Elon Musk fed it to the shredder. Related: Cascading Curruption and Incompetence: Things Fall Apart A congressional response to this global wrecking ball must certainly include rebuilding AID. Our allies must once again be treated like allies, and our adversaries must relearn how to be adversaries. Ukraine must once more be backed strongly, and Taiwan must know that we affirm that her status may not be changed by force. This self-inflicted catastrophe will take years to overcome. At first, the Democrats will lead the recovery. Beginning in January, the Democratic Congress can show that they are serious. Eventually, we hope non-MAGA Republicans will join the work. But Democrats must lead.
